Length and Distance:
📏 Length & Distance 📏

Measuring from one end to the other!

1. What is Length?

Length tells us how long an object is from one end to the other! We measure length for things like pencils, desks, and swimming pools.

2. What is Distance?

Distance tells us how far apart two places are, or how far something travels! Like walking 500 meters to the store, or driving 35 kilometers to another town.

3. The Metric Units

  • Millimeter (mm): Very tiny! Used for the thickness of a card.
  • Centimeter (cm): Small! Used for pencils and notebooks (10 mm = 1 cm).
  • Meter (m): Big! Used for the height of a door or length of a room (100 cm = 1 m).
  • Kilometer (km): Huge! Used for long journeys between towns (1,000 m = 1 km).
Mass and Weight in Everyday Contexts:
⚖️ Mass & Weight ⚖️

How much matter is packed inside an object!

1. What is Mass?

Mass tells us exactly how much matter an object contains! Every physical object has mass. A tiny apple has a mass of about 150 grams, while a heavy suitcase might have a mass of 20 kilograms.

2. Mass vs. Weight

In everyday life, people say "weight" when they mean "mass." But in science, they are different! Mass is how much stuff is in you (measured in grams and kilograms). Weight is how hard gravity is pulling down on you! (Your mass is the exact same on Earth and the Moon, but you weigh much less on the Moon because its gravity is weaker!).

3. The Units of Mass

  • Milligram (mg): Super tiny! Used for medicine or vitamins.
  • Gram (g): Small! Used for fruit or chocolate (1,000 mg = 1 g).
  • Kilogram (kg): Heavy! Used for bags of rice or your own body mass (1,000 g = 1 kg).
  • Tonne (t): Massive! Used for trucks and elephants (1,000 kg = 1 Tonne).
Capacity and Volume:
🥤 Capacity and Volume 🥤

How much space an object takes up, and how much it can hold!

1. Learning Objectives

  • Explain the meaning of capacity and volume.
  • Identify common units used to measure liquids and 3D objects.
  • Distinguish between capacity and volume.

2. What is Capacity?

Capacity is the maximum amount of liquid that a container (like a bottle, jug, or tank) can hold when it is completely full. We usually measure this in Millilitres (mL) for small cups, and Litres (L) for large bottles! (1,000 mL = 1 L).

3. What is Volume?

Volume is the amount of 3D space something occupies. Everything has volume! A solid brick takes up space, and water inside a cup takes up space. Volume is usually measured in cubic units like cubic centimetres (cm³) or cubic metres (m³).

4. What is the Difference?

Think of a huge 2-Litre water bottle. Its capacity is always 2 Litres, because that's what it can hold. But if you drink half of it, the volume of the water currently inside is only 1 Litre! The capacity didn't change, but the volume of the water did!
Standard Units of Measurement:
📏 Standard Units of Measurement 📏

The universal language of size and distance!

1. Learning Objectives

  • Explain what standard units of measurement are.
  • Understand why standard units are so important!
  • Record measurements correctly using unit symbols.

2. Why do we need Standard Units?

Imagine telling a carpenter to build a desk that is "8 handspans long." If the carpenter has giant hands, the desk will be huge! Non-standard units (like handspans, footsteps, or cups) change depending on who is measuring.

A Standard Unit is an agreed-upon measurement that is exactly the same everywhere in the world! A centimetre in London is exactly the same as a centimetre in Tokyo.

3. The Metric System Symbols

4. Rules for writing Symbols

When you write a measurement, always leave a space between the number and the symbol (write 12 cm, not 12cm). Also, never add an 's' to make it plural! (Write 5 kg, not 5 kgs).
Converting Measurement Units:
🔄 The Conversion Machine 🔄

Changing the unit without changing the actual size!

1. The Golden Rule of Conversion

When you convert a unit, the object doesn't grow or shrink! You are just describing it with a different word. 2 meters is exactly the same length as 200 centimeters.

  • Big unit to small unit: MULTIPLY! (There are many small pieces inside a big piece). 3 km × 1,000 = 3,000 meters!
  • Small unit to big unit: DIVIDE! (You are grouping small pieces into one big piece). 500 cm ÷ 100 = 5 meters!

2. Converting Time

Time is tricky because it doesn't use 10s or 1,000s! You have to use special numbers!

  • 1 Minute = 60 Seconds. (To change 3 minutes to seconds: 3 × 60 = 180 seconds).
  • 1 Hour = 60 Minutes. (To change 120 minutes to hours: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours).
  • 1 Day = 24 Hours!
Perimeter:
🚧 Perimeter 🚧

Walking around the outside fence!

1. What is Perimeter?

Perimeter is the total distance around the OUTSIDE boundary of a 2D shape. Imagine walking all the way around a garden fence until you get back to where you started!

2. How to calculate it

To find the perimeter of any polygon, just add up the lengths of all its sides!

  • Rectangle Formula: P = 2 × (Length + Width). Because a rectangle has two equal lengths and two equal widths!
  • Square Formula: P = 4 × side. Because a square has 4 perfectly equal sides! (A square with 5cm sides has a perimeter of 4 × 5 = 20cm).

3. Finding a Missing Side

If you know the perimeter of a square is 36m, how long is one side? Work backwards! Divide the perimeter by 4. 36 ÷ 4 = 9m!
Area of Squares and Rectangles:
🟦 Area 🟦

Counting the flat tiles covering the floor!

1. What is Area?

Area is the amount of flat surface covered INSIDE a shape. If you want to know how much carpet you need for a room, or how much paint you need for a wall, you calculate Area! It is always measured in Square Units (like cm² or m²).

2. The Area Formula

To find the area of a rectangle, multiply the Length by the Width! Area = L × W. If a room is 8m long and 4m wide, the area is 8 × 4 = 32 m²!

3. The Square Formula

Because a square has equal sides, you just multiply the side by itself! Area = s × s. A square garden with 7m sides has an area of 7 × 7 = 49 m²!

💡 Remember: Perimeter is the fence on the outside. Area is the grass on the inside!
Volume — Introductory:
🧊 Volume 🧊

How much space an object takes up in the 3D world!

1. What is Volume?

Volume is the amount of 3-dimensional space an object takes up! A flat drawing has area, but a real box you can hold has volume. It is always measured in Cubic Units (like cm³ or m³). Think of counting how many little 1cm blocks can fit perfectly inside a box!

2. The Volume Formula

To find the volume of a rectangular box (a cuboid), you multiply all three dimensions together: Volume = Length × Width × Height.

If a box is 4cm long, 3cm wide, and 2cm high: V = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cm³!

3. Volume vs. Capacity

Volume is the space the physical box takes up. Capacity is how much liquid the box can hold inside it! Capacity is usually measured in Liters (L) or milliliters (mL).
Estimation and Measurement Tools:
🛠️ The Right Tool for the Job 🛠️

Guessing smart, and measuring perfectly!

1. Estimation

Estimation is making a sensible, educated guess about an amount before you measure it. If you guess a pencil is 15cm, and then measure it and find it's 16cm, your estimate was great! Estimation helps you realize if your final math answer makes sense.

2. Choosing the Tool

  • Ruler: For short, straight things like pencils (cm, mm).
  • Measuring Tape: For rooms, furniture, and curved objects (m, cm).
  • Weighing Scale: For measuring the mass of objects (kg, g).
  • Measuring Jug: For measuring the volume/capacity of liquids (L, mL).
  • Stopwatch: For measuring elapsed time, like a running race (seconds, minutes).
  • Thermometer: For measuring temperature (°C).
Choosing Suitable Units:
📏 Picking the Perfect Unit 📏

Don't measure a highway with a millimeter!

1. Why does it matter?

If you say your desk is 1,500 millimeters long, people will be confused! It is much easier to say it is 1.5 meters long. Choosing the right unit makes math easy to communicate!

2. Length & Distance

  • Millimeter (mm): Thickness of a coin.
  • Centimeter (cm): Length of your shoe.
  • Meter (m): Length of a car.
  • Kilometer (km): Driving to a different city.

3. Mass & Weight

  • Milligram (mg): A grain of sand or medicine.
  • Gram (g): A strawberry.
  • Kilogram (kg): A heavy backpack.
  • Tonne (t): A blue whale!
Measurement Word Problems:
🕵️‍♂️ Measurement Mysteries 🕵️‍♀️

Putting all our measuring tools to work in the real world!

1. The Golden Rule of Word Problems

If a word problem has two different units, you MUST convert them to be the same before you add or subtract them! You cannot subtract 180cm from 5 meters directly!

2. Solving a Length Problem

"A rope is 5 m long. A piece measuring 180 cm is cut off. How much remains?"

Step 1: Convert the big unit to the small unit. 5 meters = 500 cm!

Step 2: Calculate! 500 cm − 180 cm = 320 cm. (Which is 3 meters and 20 centimeters!).

3. Solving a Time Problem

"A walk takes 25 minutes, and another walk takes 40 minutes. What is the total time?"

Step 1: Add the minutes! 25 + 40 = 65 minutes.

Step 2: Convert to hours! Since 60 minutes is 1 hour, 65 minutes is exactly 1 hour and 5 minutes!
